introduction: The Bahá’í Faith has no clergy, and these readings say why: religious leaders “appropriated all the rights and powers unto themselves”, took dress for piety, kept people from God and from knowledge, meddled in politics and resisted science; so the office itself is abolished and its work laid on every believer. The sharpest words in older scripture are aimed the same way: Ezekiel’s shepherds who feed themselves, Malachi’s priests, Jesus on those who love “the uppermost rooms at feasts” and his “all ye are brethren”, the Qur’an on rabbis and monks. Milton’s “blind mouths” is the Protestant version. The defence of priesthood is heard from Hebrews, where no one takes the honour “but he that is called of God”; Chaucer’s parson stands for the good priest reading 12 allows; and Paine shows where rejection of clergy can end.
questions: List the faults these readings find in clergy. Which belong to the office and which to human nature in any position of trust?
“All ye are brethren.” Why did communities founded on that saying develop hierarchies, and what in the Bahá’í arrangement is meant to prevent it?
Reading 20 says each believer must do what priests did. What exactly were those services?
Hebrews holds that true priests are called by God. How would the readings distinguish a calling from a caste?

outside.why: The garb of the learned taken as a sign of piety. All their works they do for to be seen of men: they make broad their phylacteries, and love the uppermost rooms at feasts.
The ordained man thinks he knows more of God; the humble man in the congregation may know more. The publican went down to his house justified rather than the other.
Self-seeking leaders who took all rights to themselves. Woe be to the shepherds of Israel that do feed themselves! should not the shepherds feed the flocks?
They bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men’s shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with one of their fingers.
It profits religious leaders to keep imitations alive. Milton on the clergy of his day: blind mouths! The hungry sheep look up, and are not fed.
Priests who became self-centred. The priest’s lips should keep knowledge; but ye are departed out of the way; ye have caused many to stumble at the law.
A barrier between God and His loved ones. They be blind leaders of the blind. And if the blind lead the blind, both shall fall into the ditch.
Know thyself more learned than the turbaned who disbelieved. Not many wise men after the flesh, not many mighty, are called.
Priests attached to old superstitions. The Qur’an: many of the rabbis and the monks devour the wealth of mankind wantonly and debar men from the way of Allah.

Some popes were blessed souls who followed Christ. Chaucer, who spares few of his churchmen, drew one good priest: first he wrought, and afterward he taught. Does the guide’s criticism fall on the office or on those who abuse it?
Their meddling in politics brought their own abasement. Man, who made me a judge or a divider over you?
A hierarchy that reversed Christ’s teaching of unity. Be not ye called Rabbi: for one is your Master, and all ye are brethren. And call no man your father upon the earth.

“Let thine abode be under the stone, but seek not the shelter of the cleric.” Paine went further: my own mind is my own church. The readings abolish priests and keep a religion, with its institutions. What is the difference?

Religious offices uprooted. Hebrews defends a priesthood by divine call: no man taketh this honour unto himself, but he that is called of God, as was Aaron. And when Korah argued that “all the congregation are holy”, the book of Numbers took Moses’s side. How do the readings answer the claim that some are set apart?
No special caste; knowledge for all. Moses: would God that all the Lord’s people were prophets, and that the Lord would put his spirit upon them!
“We have no priests”; each believer renders the service priests once did. Ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood.

Every believer is to teach. Paul’s letters, which also speak of bishops and elders, put it as a chain: the same commit thou to faithful men, who shall be able to teach others also. Without clergy, who makes sure this is done?
